narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Observatory Console"**

Ara looks like the dark instrument panel at the telescope. Surfaces are neutral greys stepped a few points apart. Information is dense, in the NINA tradition: small type, tight spacing, panels separated by hairline borders. Colour belongs to the equipment and the session. A green dot means connected, amber means busy or needs a look, red means fault or stop. Nothing else is coloured. At rest the screen is quiet, so a change of state is the loudest thing on it.

One idea is borrowed from a cockpit. When something needs the person (often checking in at 3 a.m.), it must be impossible to miss: icon, colour and words together, never colour alone. Emergency Stop is the heaviest control on every screen. Controls behave like labelled hardware: switches name their states, readouts carry a status dot, and numbers use tabular figures so they don't jitter while they update.

The app runs on Material 3 (dark) with the Ara tokens below, on desktop and mobile, so the UI must survive Night mode. Night mode folds every pixel's luminance into the red channel, and the interface then reads by brightness alone.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral grey surfaces with tonal steps and 1 px borders; no shadows.
Colour only through semantic status roles, never as decoration.
Dense, small type ramp (11–15 px) on one spacing scale (4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24).
Attention states are unmissable: icon + colour + text.
Emergency Stop: filled red, always visible, on every tab.
Instrument-like controls: named switch states, status dots, tabular numbers.
Two densities: the dense full UI, and a roomy, image-first Simple Mode (the frame fills the screen; controls float on translucent overlays; 44 px targets, 10 px corners, 14 px type).

rules.name: The State-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: An accent appears only through a semantic role: a state dot, a state chip, a category hue or a destructive action. If it doesn't mean something, it is grey.

rules.name: The Brightness-First Rule
rules.body: Every state must still read in Night mode, where hue is gone and only luminance remains. A connected dot must stay brighter than a border. Never tell two states apart by hue alone.

rules.name: The Steady Digits Rule
rules.body: Every number that updates live uses tabular figures. A countdown never shifts its neighbours.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: New and redesigned surfaces use the `AraText` ramp above, not per-widget 11/12/13 px styles. The ramp is being adopted incrementally, and older widgets still carry ad-hoc sizes (12 px is common).

rules.name: The Two Densities Rule
rules.body: The full UI is dense: 11–15 px type and 4–8 px corners. Simple Mode is roomy and image-first: the frame fills the window, controls float on translucent overlays, every interactive target is at least 44 px tall, corners are 10 px, and body text is 14 px. Both densities share the same colours, the same named rules and the same Emergency Stop hold; both densities' Stop fills with `emergency-stop` (#D32F2F) so its label reads at 4.5:1. Phones run Companion Mode, which builds on Simple Mode, so phones always get the roomy density. Simple Mode ships on master behind an experimental toggle (Settings → System → Experimental); this is its target.

rules.name: The Start-Stops Rule
rules.body: Whatever starts something also stops it: the shutter that starts a shot, a loop or a routine turns into a red square that stops it, and an Autofocus button turns into Cancel. No second Stop button sits beside it. Simple Mode's Plan is the one variant: a plan runs a whole night, so its shutter starts the plan (a play triangle in a white ring, like every mode but Preview), then pauses it (pause bars), resumes it (a play triangle in an amber ring), and a 2 s hold stops it. In Simple Mode, Done is green (Connected Green), as the one completing action; the full UI keeps its default Done (decided 2026-11-02: the full UI stays as it is).

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces don't cast shadows or glow. A panel is separated by a 1 px Hairline and a tonal step, nothing more. The exceptions are Simple Mode's overlays, which float over the image on a translucent scrim, still with no shadow, and a gold Sky Album Card, which carries a soft gold glow (8 px blur at 35 %) as the top tier's reward (decided 2026-11-06, as the album spec asks); bronze and silver Cards do not glow.

rules.name: Simple Mode's rule: 4×90% and KISS
rules.body: Simple Mode covers the top 90 % most used features, for 90 % of the people, 90 % of the time, 90 % faster, with only the bare minimum for a successful imaging night: defaults and automation first, self-recovery doing the work, and a small set of controls where the user needs them (ASIAir as the reference); a value one Simple Mode control sets is not repeated elsewhere, and nothing links to the full UI. No redundant design: each thing lives in one place, and interactions are contextual (tap the thing to act on it). Its Settings (a sheet over the image with a few controls, ASIAir as the reference; one window per device, the same one its top-bar dot opens; Connect / Disconnect on Settings › Devices only) are shaped in `design/briefs/simple-mode-settings.md` (2026-11-03).

rules.name: The Brand Stays Home Rule
rules.body: The brand palette lives in two places, the Ara mark and the no-frame wallpaper. It never marks a state, a selection or a call to action.

rules.name: The Drawings Stay Grey Rule
rules.body: Device-window drawings (the dome clamshell and dial, the flat panel face) use their own grey ramp: dome body #808080 to #4A4A4A, shells #A8A8A8 to #6A6A6A, plinth #8A8A8A, hinge bolt #D0D0D0, dial slit #6E6E6E at 95 %, flat panel face #111111, lids #303030, ribs #242424, glow #FFFBE8 to #B8B29A. They picture hardware and never mark a state; a state on a drawing comes only from a status token.

dos: **Do** pair every warning or fault with icon + colour + text. Colour alone never carries a message.
**Do** keep Emergency Stop filled red, visible on every tab and heavier than any other control.
**Do** use `AraColors`, `AraSpace` and `AraText` tokens. Accents come only through semantic roles.
**Do** use tabular figures for any live number.
**Do** check every new state in Night mode: it must still be distinguishable by brightness.

**Do** meet WCAG 2.2 AA on every new or changed control (playbook §53): 4.5:1 text, keyboard reach with visible focus, a pointer-free path for every hold or drag. Night mode is exempt from contrast; the default theme isn't.
**Do** write labels in product voice: verbs, sentence case, no NINA or daemon enum names.
donts: **Don't** change the full UI's layout while Simple Mode is being built. Simple Mode is additive: new work goes into Simple Mode, and the full UI (PR #1474's shell) stays as it is for now. Two exceptions are approved: the heavier Emergency Stop (ALP-4812), which applies to the full UI too, and a Simple Mode icon in the full UI's top-right cluster, between Night mode and the gear (decided 2026-11-01).

**Don't** use colour for decoration, branding flourishes or emphasis that isn't a state. The one exception is the brand palette (`AraColors.brand*`, the app icon's navy and line blues): only the OpenAstro Ara mark and Simple Mode's no-frame wallpaper use it (approved 2026-11-05, #1602).
**Don't** add shadows or glows to separate surfaces; use a tonal step and a Hairline.
**Don't** let any state fall back to plain grey text without a designed look.
**Don't** fill any control other than Emergency Stop and confirmed destructive actions with Fault Red.
**Don't** copy NINA's icons, splash, imagery or wordmark (see PRODUCT.md).
**Don't** hard-code colours outside `lib/theme/`. A few widgets still do, and they should migrate to tokens.
